BiblicalUsage: I take gêʼeh to mean proud, nothing more and nothing less. It occurs 8 times, and Job and Psalms show it doing ordinary work in ordinary sentences. The Bible uses plain words plainly, and this is one of them.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that gêʼeh matters because pride is the sin that stands furthest from God. My position is that Scripture does not hide its meaning from honest readers.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
